reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the narrator urges viewers to put at least $100 in Bitcoin into a trading pool and presents it as a way to relax while their Bitcoin grows daily, citing roughly 0.5% average daily profit and stories of members paying expenses. The website's warning that past results do not guarantee future returns is present, but the narrator's repeated easy-income assurances and invitation to join dominate the message. The shown opportunity also offers bonuses tied to building a two-leg recruiting team.

citations.quote: When you register with Maior trading International, you can join with a minimum of $100 worth of Bitcoin which will go into a trading pool. From there, it is traded on your behalf. So no trading knowledge is necessary at all.
The historic results show an average daily profit of 0.5%. However, historic results are poorly indicative of the past trading results, and there are no guarantees of future results.
Once your Bitcoin is received in your MTI account your Bitcoin from part of the total Trading Pool then you can sit back, relax and watch your Bitcoin grow daily. Amazing thing, right?

opening.argument: The presentation expressly distinguishes historical performance from any promise of future results. It reports an historical average, then immediately qualifies that information by stating that past results are not reliable indicators and that future returns are not guaranteed. That is a material risk warning, not a certification of safe profit. The language also explains the arrangement rather than concealing uncertainty: funds are placed into a pool and traded on the participant’s behalf. A careful viewer is therefore told both the claimed historical figure and the limitation on relying upon it. The existence of optimistic phrasing does not erase an explicit non-guarantee, especially where the speaker does not state that viewers will actually earn the cited percentage.

citations.quote: The historic results show an average daily profit of 0.5%. However, historic results are poorly indicative of the past trading results, and there are no guarantees of future results.
When you register with Maior trading International, you can join with a minimum of $100 worth of Bitcoin which will go into a trading pool.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes the minimum contribution and optimistic language, but those points do not establish a guaranteed return. Its own cited material contains the direct qualification that historical results are not indicative and future results are not guaranteed. “Watch your Bitcoin grow” is promotional encouragement, but it does not negate the express warning or prove that the speaker concealed risk. Stories about expenses likewise do not establish that every viewer will receive those outcomes.

citations.quote: However, historic results are poorly indicative of the past trading results, and there are no guarantees of future results.
Here how people are now able to pay other monthly expenses on time, pay schools fees, make purchases they only dreamt of before

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not neutralize the presentation’s central solicitation. The same passage pairs the warning with a specific average daily profit, while the speaker repeatedly describes effortless growth and urges viewers toward a minimum Bitcoin contribution. The qualification says only that past results do not guarantee future results; it does not verify the trading, explain the pool’s safeguards, or make the promised opportunity ordinary. In context, the warning is outweighed by the repeated easy-income framing.

citations.quote: The historic results show an average daily profit of 0.5%.
you can sit back, relax and watch your Bitcoin grow daily
So you can chill out. You can relax because your Bitcoin is growing

opening.argument: The video can reasonably be understood as a review and operational walkthrough rather than a direct financial solicitation. Its title explicitly calls itself a review, and the narrator spends substantial time navigating the site and explaining how the claimed system works: membership access, automated trading, trading statements, software, and withdrawal processing. That is explanatory content giving viewers information to assess, not evidence that the presenter personally guarantees the service. The narration describes the claimed mechanics and available features, including that no trading knowledge is required and that users can move funds. A demonstration of a website’s stated process should not automatically be treated as proof that the presenter is endorsing every claim or guaranteeing an outcome.

citations.quote: Mirror Trading International Review- Relax and Grow your Bitcoin!!
At first go to the menu panel. On the home it says about overview, contact, become a member and members login.
MTE uses Mt4 Software and trades is affected by it debat.
withdraw request are processed within 48 hours

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a review does not make it neutral, but the supplied narration still functions as an explanation of the website and its claimed operations. It does not identify the speaker’s relationship to the service, show a completed registration, or document a payment or realized return. Describing what the site says is materially different from independently certifying it. The reference’s inference of endorsement therefore goes beyond what the recording itself establishes.

citations.quote: Mirror Trading International Review- Relax and Grow your Bitcoin!!
On the home it says about overview, contact, become a member and members login.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title’s use of “Review” does not control the video’s substance. The narrator repeatedly praises the opportunity, calls it amazing, tells viewers they can relax while Bitcoin grows, and describes people paying expenses through it. Explaining the registration and trading process is precisely how a promotional solicitation can be made accessible. The absence of proof that a transaction occurred does not change the invitation to place Bitcoin into the pool or the presentation of effortless returns.

citations.quote: Here is Kylas and today I will tell you about a very amazing thing!
you can sit back, relax and watch your Bitcoin grow daily
it is already starting to change lives everyday

opening.argument: The material describes a purported automated trading service with ordinary operational features, not a demonstrated scam mechanism. It explains that Bitcoin is traded on the participant’s behalf, that daily statements are provided, that users may read out their funds, and that withdrawal requests are processed within 48 hours. The evidence does not show the narrator requesting passwords, seed phrases, bank credentials, or other sensitive information. Nor does the narration promise a fixed or guaranteed return; it expressly says future results are not guaranteed. Referral language appears as an optional program, but the core explanation is still a service description. On this record, the claims may deserve independent research, yet the video does not establish deception or a missing service.

citations.quote: From there, it is traded on your behalf. So no trading knowledge is necessary at all.
you will receive a trading statement the following day, detailing the traders and the profit made.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The presence of ordinary-sounding features does not prove the service exists or performs as described, but it also does not itself show a scam. The reference identifies a deposit and projected returns, yet the record does not show credentials being requested, a completed payment, or an actual failed withdrawal. Referral language is described as optional, and the narration does not explain a tiered structure. Those evidentiary gaps matter when deciding whether the video establishes deception rather than merely repeating a service’s claims.

citations.quote: Mta will also have a limited live view of trades taking place
withdraw request are processed within 48 hours

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam need not request passwords or show a completed loss in the video. The central mechanism is explicit: viewers are asked to place at least $100 worth of Bitcoin into a pooled account, with the service claiming passive daily growth. The alleged statements, live view, and withdrawal timing are unverified claims presented as reassurance, not independent proof. The supplied page also shows bonus terms tied to investment volume in a weakest leg, reinforcing that this is more than ordinary retail commerce.
